purpose: Illustrated Ink replay segmentation and image prompt controls for a 2091 Horizon Ventures habitat default at Mare Crisium Receiving Cylinder.

visual_scene_plan.purpose: Click-through visual anchors for the lunar cylinder, ordinary seal and breakfast work, four routine choices, continuity-default classification, the false-green hatch failure, final priority, and four ending families.
visual_scene_plan.segmentation_rule: Use separate visual_scene_id anchors for exterior locality, gallery layout, hatch closeup, breakfast relationships, each routine branch, ordinary fold, amber default notice, classified queue, false-green pressure failure, final threshold, and each ending family. The default notice and falling pressure gauge stand as separate pivotal replay beats.
visual_scene_plan.prompting_rule: Each base image prompt is a complete visible frame for a general image model: camera, lunar or interior geometry, materials, practical lighting, bodies, clothing, tools, interfaces, and consequential objects are stated directly. Character refs are assembled only for people visible in the frame.
visual_scene_plan.global_style_cue: Humane retro-industrial science-fiction storybook illustration, precise dark ink linework under thin gouache color, cold lunar grays and hard white dock light interrupted by amber alarms and warm food-cart steam, readable silhouettes and mechanical interfaces, tactile worn materials, restrained facial acting, cinematic composition for bleak workplace drama.
visual_scene_plan.prompt_assembly_rule: Assemble each prompt from global_style_cue, the selected scene base_image_prompt, visual refs only for named characters or groups listed as visible in that frame, and triggered state_image_modifiers or global_branch_image_modifiers. Continuity notes remain tooling constraints. Camera-specific blockout input is required for high-consistency multi-angle renders.

scenes.base_image_prompt: Wide exterior view on the lunar surface in 2091: Mare Crisium Receiving Cylinder is a long horizontal pressurized metal habitat half-buried in pale regolith, with ribbed pressure sections, radiator panels, cable trenches, repair sheds, and a compact landing pad attached to one end. A small insured shuttle waits under hard white floodlights beside cargo pallets. Black sky, harsh shadows, dust-scoured gray plating, tiny suited workers, and a low compact silhouette establish a sparse industrial facility.

visible_characters.default_stance: tiny suited figures tending cargo pallets and pad connections

visual_continuity_notes: The cylinder is a lunar surface habitat with one attached transfer gallery and pad, not a rotating orbital habitat.
The shuttle remains physically outside the dockward collar throughout the gallery scene.

scenes.base_image_prompt: Wide interior view down Transfer Gallery Two inside a lunar freight habitat: gray floor grating runs in a straight line from a heavy habitatward pressure hatch in the near wall to a circular dockward collar and pad window at the far end. A recessed manifest desk occupies the right wall; a sealed glass audit booth occupies the left wall facing it. Yellow cargo-grid paint marks the dock end. Exposed red pressure pipes, a waist-high bypass cabinet, analog gauge, overhead cable trays, and amber-white work lamps make every system reachable and worn. The waiting shuttle is visible through the far window.
visual_continuity_notes: Habitatward and dockward form one stable straight coordinate axis.
Manifest desk remains gallery-right; glass audit booth remains gallery-left; bypass cabinet and honest gauge remain beside Hatch MCR-2.

scenes.base_image_prompt: Close-medium maintenance view at the habitatward end of Transfer Gallery Two: Sera Madani, a lean brown-skinned baseline human woman in her late thirties with tightly braided black hair, orange-gray seal-technician coveralls, paper credential cuff, tool belt, and heavy low-gravity work boots, braces one boot on a chalk mark over gray floor grating. She drives a waist-high steel dog handle through a second closure stroke on a thick pressure hatch labeled MCR-2. The electronic panel already glows green while an analog needle beside the red pressure pipe is still settling. Scuffed seals, worn lower linkage, amber work lamp, and paper checklist make the discrepancy visible.

visible_characters.default_stance: boot on chalk brace, both hands driving the second stroke

visual_continuity_notes: The dog handle is waist-high and operated by bracing against the floor, not by kicking the hatch panel.
